Priya: Quick flag from onboarding Nebula-7B -> int4: generation quality is fine short (<1024) but collapses for 4k+ contexts. FP16 ppl 10.8, int4 ppl jumps to 16.7 at 4096+. Anyone seen this pattern? :eyes:
Marcus: Could be rotary aliasing or a vocab offset. Do we have conversion logs and tokenizer seed?
Priya: Conversion command used: 
```
python tools/convert_model.py --src nebula7b/ --dst converted/nebula7b-int4/ --quant int4 --backend gptq
```
Output had an innocuous warning: "rotary_base not found, defaulting to 10000" but model config shows base=1000.
Lina: base=1000 vs default 10000 would drastically change freq sampling. That explains aliasing at earlier positions (wraps sooner).
Sam: Also noticed many samples with embedded flags/emoji shift the token indices by +1 for a stretch, as if a sentinel token sneaks in. Example tokenizer.encode: 
```
>>> tokenizer.encode("flag: \ud83c\udff3\ufe0f\u200d\u26a7\ufe0f hello")
[4096, 0, 0, 3456, 78]
```
Those zeros are not real pads in training — they're splitted ZWJ components.
Marcus: That could create off-by-one for embeddings if the converter wrote a different vocab order. Are we preserving tokenizer.vocab and merges exactly?
Priya: Converter wrote a vocab.json but our tokenization tests show normalization mismatch: model trained on NFKC, converter pipeline used NFC. So ZWJ sequences split.
Jorge: And if rotor base mismatch + token id shift both occur, the KV cache and rotary phase alignment will no longer match, causing catastrophic errors for long context.
Lina: I ran a headwise phase probe: 
```
python tools/rotary_check.py --model converted/nebula7b-int4/ --input tests/long_news.txt --maxlen 8192
```
Results: 
```
[INFO] head 0..2 ok
[WARN] head 4: phase_wrap @ pos 1024 -> delta 0.34 rad
[WARN] head 9: alias @ pos 1536 -> wrap
```
That aligns with base=1000 (wrap sooner).
Marcus: Two-pronged fix: 1) ensure converter reads rotary_emb.base and rotary_emb.scale (look for aliases: rotary_base, rotary_emb.base, rotary.base), 2) enforce tokenizer normalization to NFKC during conversion and add emoji/ZWJ merge rules.
Sam: I tried forcing base=1000 in converted config and re-running a small eval: ppl dropped from 16.7 -> 13.9 for longctx but still above fp16 10.8.
Priya: Did you also try switching gptq quant options? Per-head scale can matter.
Sam: Yup. Re-converted with gptq per-channel scales preserved: 
```
python tools/convert_model.py --src nebula7b/ --dst converted/nebula7b-int4-perhead/ --quant int4 --backend gptq --preserve-perhead-scale --preserve-rotary
```
That improved ppl to 12.1 and removed phase_wrap. Latency unchanged.
Jorge: Good. On tokenizer side, I wrote a small sanitizer: 
```
def sanitize(text):
    text = unicodedata.normalize('NFKC', text)
    text = merge_known_emoji_sequences(text)
    return text
```
Applying this before tokenization fixed the zero-token artefacts in our test set.
Lina: Action items: patch converter to recognize rotary_emb.base/rotary_base aliases and add `--preserve-rotary` flag (PR in review), add `--preserve-perhead-scale` for gptq, and update default tokenizer pipeline to run NFKC normalization for onboards.
Marcus: I'll add a unit test that simulates ZWJ emoji + validation that vocab roundtrips to converted vocab.json exactly. Also add a regression test for headwise phase deltas >0.05 rad.
Infra Bot: artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-artifacts/eng-ml/1719999998/nebula-convert-logs.tar.gz :white_check_mark:
Priya: Let's also add a small CI job that runs `rotary_check.py` on new models with a 8k synthetic long context and fail the onboard if headwise wrap detected.
Sam: Note: even after fixes, summarization ROUGE dropped ~2.2 pts in a few datasets. We'll keep the model in dedicated staging and run full eval suite.
Jorge: Filing follow-ups: RED-2145 (converter rotary aliases), RED-2146 (tokenizer normalization+emoji merges), RED-2147 (gptq per-head scale support).
Priya: Thanks all. Saved a painful promote-to-dedicated mistake. :sparkles:
Marcus: :thumbsup:
